correctness.rationale: On im(t), t is an involution by t^3=t, so every other point is one step from a fixed point or two-cycle. The law et=e makes e constant on each t-component, te=e puts each target at a t-fixed vertex, and e^2=e makes that target its own image. Thus a fiber of e is precisely a distinguished rooted star and a multiset of other stars and two-cycle components; fibers themselves form an unordered multiset. For size j>=2, the unordered leaf-count pairs with sum j-2 yield floor(j/2) two-cycle types. Excluding every such type is exactly the t=t^2 condition; hence the subtraction of Euler transforms counts all and only the rank-three compatible-pair orbits. There is no t^2=e cancellation when t!=t^2, since then te=t^3=t would force e=t. The formal logarithmic derivative gives both divisor recurrences. The cited classification and essentiality apply in the claimed n>=5 generator regime; small-index coefficients have the compatible-pair interpretation.
residual_risks: Finite recomputations corroborate the bijection but do not establish the all-size claim; that rests on the component proof and the cited classification. No full generator enumeration is asserted.
